name: node is now needed to write, check or remove the start-up block
why: Not exercised by a golden scenario (the base side needs no node); pinned by the declared test in shell-rc-golden.test.js. The rc_* and shell_rc_* functions were shell and awk, so the block was handled whatever node there was. startup_step runs src/render/shell-rc.js on the node the settings merge runs (allow_node, the same lookup: MHW_NODE, an absolute path, else node on PATH, refused when it is not an executable file or does not run as node). Without one it prints 'REFUSE  the shell start-up block: <reason>; no start-up file changed', raises 2 and changes no file, in every mode. On install and check this changes nothing in practice: the block is written only where the paste wrapper's snippet is, and the snippet already needs that node. On uninstall it does: without a node the block stays in the start-up file, and the list of files install created stays in the data directory, so the data directory is not removed either. The block stays harmless: it sources the snippet only when it is readable ('[ -r ... ] &&'), and uninstall_user removes the snippet. settings.json is left the same way by the same missing node (#491).

name: a write that fails stops the installer with one REFUSE line
why: Not exercised by a golden scenario (the shell side's messages are its tools' own and differ between Apple and GNU); pinned in shell-rc.test.js and by the declared test in shell-rc-golden.test.js. When the backup, a directory, the created-files list or the start-up file itself could not be written, rc_write stopped install.sh at once under set -e, exit 1, with private_copy's REFUSE line or the message of mkdir, mktemp or the shell's redirection (a failed mktemp printed no REFUSE line at all). The Node step prints 'REFUSE  <file>.pmhwc-backup: the backup could not be created exclusively; no backup written' or 'REFUSE  <file>: could not be written (<error>)' on stderr and exits 4, and startup_step then exits 1 at once, as before: nothing after it runs. As before, a backup written before a failed write stays.

name: an unreadable start-up file is refused, and the later steps still run
why: Not exercised by a golden scenario (the shell side's message is awk's own); pinned in shell-rc.test.js. Measured on the base revision with a 0000 ~/.zshrc: rc_scan's awk printed 'awk: can't open file <file>' and the failed command substitution stopped install.sh under set -e, exit 2, in install and in uninstall alike, so nothing after the step ran (on uninstall: uninstall_user and the method step). The Node step prints 'REFUSE  <file>: cannot be read (EACCES); nothing written' (or 'nothing removed' on uninstall), raises 3 and leaves the file as it was, and the installer's later steps run, as they do after the other REFUSE lines of this step.

name: an unforeseen failure of the step is a refusal
why: Not exercised by a scenario. Exit 1 is drift under --check only; elsewhere it is node's own exit code for an uncaught exception, so startup_step reads it as a refusal (raise 3), and shell-rc.js catches anything unforeseen itself: 'REFUSE  the shell start-up block: the step failed (<error>); the file it was on is left as it was', exit 3. The shell functions had no such case (an error stopped install.sh under set -e). Pinned by the declared exit-code test in shell-rc-golden.test.js.

name: install.sh --help names the Node step
why: Not exercised by a scenario. The --shell-rc paragraph of install.sh's usage text (printed by -h) named the removed function rc_bash_login for the macOS login-file rule; it now names src/render/shell-rc.js. The help still prints the same lines 2 to 36.
